description:
Survey and write up (docs/research/multilingual-sota.md) the state of the art and its applicability under WebNN on a flagship phone. Answer: can we (C) completely mix languages, (B) detect per spoken line, or only (A) select a language? Starting points from an initial search (2026-09-13):
- Unified multilingual models are generally favored over cascade LID-then-route for code-switching; cascades are OK for clean inter-sentential boundaries (Gladia/Deepgram guides). Intra-utterance switching remains much harder (~41% WER for a lightweight ensemble vs ~26% for best cloud).
- Qwen3-ASR (0.6B/1.7B, already our final STT default): 52 languages, LID via prompting before decoding (~98% avg LID acc for 1.7B), claims in-file language-switch handling; ForcedAligner supports code-switched alignment. arXiv 2601.21337.
- NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 ASR Streaming 0.6B (FastConformer-RNNT, cache-aware, 80–1120 ms chunks, 40 locales, target_lang=auto per-utterance LID, OpenMDW license; no documented ONNX, code-switching not documented). Candidate live multilingual model.
- Moonshine Streaming: monolingual checkpoints (en + ar/zh/ja/ko/uk/vi etc.) => only mode A/B via routing.
- Whisper: LID per 30 s window, poor at intra-window switching; Whisper Small/Tiny are current auto fallbacks.
- Standalone LID: SpeechBrain ECAPA-TDNN VoxLingua107 (107 langs, strong baseline, TidyLang 2026), ESPnet MMS-1B+ECAPA LID (heavier); frame-level LID / language diarization (DISPLACE challenge, token-level language diarization).
- Soniox stt-rt-v5: token-level LID with sentence-level coherence, mid-sentence switching without restarts, 60+ languages.
- Datasets: CS-FLEURS (2025), SwitchLingua (2025, 12 langs), MLC-SLM; arXiv 2606.05846 shows CS ability transfers only modestly to unseen pairs; arXiv 2605.19069 benchmarks commercial CS ASR; arXiv 2507.07741 CS E2E ASR survey.
Deliverable: comparison table (model, languages, LID granularity, CS support, streaming, size, license, ONNX/WebNN status) and a recommended mode for live and final passes.
title: Research: SOTA survey of multilingual, LID, and code-switched ASR for on-device use
